chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Playing for fraternal orders on trips, with Mrs. Allen's discipline
summary: The band played marches for the Elks, Masons and United Brothers of Friendship, travelled to Chicago and St. Louis, was cheap because non-union, and was put up in dormitories under strict supervision.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And they were always bringing in new music books, marches, you know, which we didn't play in Sunday School -- we'd play those marches in front of fraternal organizations, you know.
Oh, like the Elks and everything?
Like the Elks and Masons and the United Brothers of Friendship. And sometimes they would go on a convention, and they would take us because they could get us cheaper, see.
Yes.
Once we went to Chicago, and St. Louis. I think the Elks took us to St. Louis. And they could get us -- see the men, they wanted a certain price, you know.
Yeah.
And they could get us cheaper.
Yeah.
Because we didn't belong to no union.
No.
And they'd get the whole gang and put us all in a big dormitory.
Yeah.
They didn't have to worry about no rooms
for us, with all these beds in here, all these cots, you know.
Yeah, sure.
Yeah.
That's where the band was.

Yeah, sure. And I was trying to think were there any girls there. I can't think -- I know they were there, because I have a picture there with them on it. But I -- maybe they stayed somewhere else, because you know how kids are in those days.
That's right.
So I imagine some of the girls' parents wouldn't have agreed to all staying together like that.
Yeah, that's right.
But she was very strict. So things went down right. She was strict, yeah.
It was done just like it should be.
Yes, she was very strict. No -- you couldn't get out of order or nothing, you know. Everything had to be straight.
Well, like with the band, weren't there any bad boys, or were --
Oh, yeah, we had --
